items.caption:
Cabo Girão by boat from Funchal, Madeira: six seconds of cliff, and two yellow dots.

The dots are buoys. Look just above the middle of the water, side by side, like two small eyes keeping watch on the beach.

Behind them: a strip of grey pebbles, then terraces with a few flat roofs and stone walls, then rock in red and green all the way up and out of the frame. The camera gave up before the cliff did.

Nobody built those terraces for the view. They got it anyway.

Duas boias, uma praia, e uma montanha por cima.

Both our trips come along here from the marina. The Day Trip stops at Fajã dos Padres for the swim and paddle, the Sunset Trip turns at Cabo Girão as the light goes. Your group only, five at most.

Six seconds is the Reel. The boat gives you a bit longer. Book direct on chifbay.com

items.caption:
Private boat trip from Funchal, Madeira: this is the view from the nose of our boat.

Two steel rails, a grey deck pad and a great deal of blue. Not a single thing in the way.

From out here you notice what the island is really made of: steps. Hotels on the rock, houses on the terraces, every garden with a view and a staircase.

This coast is the start of both our trips, the Day Trip and the Sunset Trip, out of Funchal marina towards Câmara de Lobos and Cabo Girão. Just your group on board, never more than five.

Mar azul, céu azul, e nós no meio.

Front seat or back seat, your call. Book direct on chifbay.com

Four friends, a boat to themselves and a cliff in Madeira: spot the one who has just been in the water.

Easy. Two towels, one hand still on the rail, and the biggest smile on board.

The other three already have their glasses back. Rosé, crisps, a tin of something, and a wooden table that stays flat while the sea does not.

Behind them the cliff goes up in stripes, red and grey and black, straight out of deep blue water.

Primeiro o mar, depois o copo.

That is the order on our Day Trip: the swim and paddle stop at Fajã dos Padres, then food on the table. Just your group, five at most, and the skipper takes the photos.

Towel first or glass first? WhatsApp us and we will find you a date.

Private boat trip under the cliffs of Madeira. Look top left: there is a road up there.

Cars crossing that bridge get a cliff and a slice of sea. Down here you get the whole wall, stripes of red, grey and black, straight into dark blue water.

Towels out, hair still wet, one hand up on the canopy pole. On the table: crisps, a wooden bowl, and something pink in most of the glasses.

The canopy says Chifbay.com, so this photo already knows where it came from.

This is our Day Trip: the swim and paddle stop at Fajã dos Padres, then food on board as we follow the coast. Just your group, no one else on the boat.

Sol na cara, sal no cabelo.

Road or water, which side would you rather be on? Details and dates on chifbay.com

Boat trip along the Madeira cliffs: find the pink wall at the bottom of this one.

It is tiny. A strip of terraces, a few fences, a pebble beach, and above it a wall of rock that fills the whole frame.

Look at the stripes. Red, yellow, grey, green, all running straight down, like somebody dragged a wet brush over the cliff and let it drip.

From the road you see the top of this. From the water you see the whole thing, and you see that someone still farms the one flat bit at the bottom.

Uma parede de pedra, e alguém ainda planta ali.

Both our trips follow this coast from Funchal marina towards Cabo Girão, just your group on the boat and a skipper who knows where the colours are best.

Want to see the stripes up close? Send us a message and we will check the dates for you.

Private boat tours from Funchal, Madeira: meet the whole crew. Both of them.

Two black polos, one wheel. Look closely: there is a hand from each of us on it. We have not settled who is driving either.

Over the shoulder on the left, a tiny parasail hangs in the sky. From the helm it looks like a small balloon somebody let go of.

The sky is grey and white, the sea is grey and blue. The boat does not care about that, and neither do we.

Dois skippers, um leme.

That is the team: two skippers, one Karnic R8S, and your group of five at most. Day Trip or Sunset Trip, it is one of these two faces at the wheel, and nobody else on board.

Next time you walk past the marina, the black polos are easy to spot. Come and say olá.

Private boat trip out of Funchal, Madeira: the town is behind us and the glasses are still empty.

Two white glasses on the edge of the boat, a bottle in the bucket, and a trail of foam where we have just been.

Look at Funchal from here. The whole town sits on a slope, as if somebody tipped the island towards the sea and the houses slid down as far as the harbour wall.

The glasses are not glass, by the way. White plastic, so they look smarter than they are. Real glass and a wake like that do not get along.

Funchal a ficar pequeno, o mar a ficar grande.

Both our trips leave from Marina do Funchal and head this way, west along the coast. Day Trip with the swim stop at Fajã dos Padres, or Sunset Trip as the light goes, and food on board on either one.

We keep it to five people on board. Send us your dates and we will tell you what is free.
